problem.statement_clinical: Hypercholesterolemia, LDL 158 mg/dL, no prior cardiovascular event

subjective.term: Family history of premature cardiovascular disease
subjective.vernacular: Has anyone in your close family (parents, siblings) had a heart attack or stroke before age 55 (men) or 65 (women)?
subjective.why_it_matters: Premature family ASCVD history significantly increases 10-year risk and lowers the threshold for statin therapy.

subjective.term: Dietary pattern — saturated and trans fat intake
subjective.vernacular: How often do you eat red meat, fried foods, full-fat dairy, or packaged snacks with partially hydrogenated oils?
subjective.why_it_matters: High saturated and trans fat intake is a primary modifiable driver of elevated LDL and supports dietary hypercholesterolemia as the leading cause.

subjective.vernacular: How many days per week do you do at least 30 minutes of moderate exercise, like brisk walking?
subjective.why_it_matters: Sedentary lifestyle lowers HDL and can raise LDL; improvement is a first-line non-pharmacological intervention.
subjective.value: Active goal to increase physical activity exists (2024-07-08); actual current activity level unknown

subjective.vernacular: Do you smoke cigarettes or use any tobacco or nicotine products currently, or did you quit within the last year?
subjective.why_it_matters: Current smoking is an independent ASCVD risk factor that materially raises 10-year risk and lowers the statin-initiation threshold.

subjective.vernacular: How many alcoholic drinks do you typically have per week?
subjective.why_it_matters: Excessive alcohol raises triglycerides and can secondarily elevate total cholesterol; it also affects medication tolerance.

subjective.vernacular: Have you noticed unusual fatigue, feeling cold all the time, unexplained weight gain, constipation, or dry skin and hair?
subjective.why_it_matters: Hypothyroidism is a common secondary cause of elevated LDL that must be excluded before primary hypercholesterolemia is assumed.

subjective.vernacular: Have you or any doctor noticed yellowish fatty deposits on your eyelids, elbows, knees, or tendons?
subjective.why_it_matters: Tendon xanthomas are pathognomonic for familial hypercholesterolemia (FH), a high-severity genetic cause requiring aggressive treatment.

subjective.vernacular: Have you ever taken a cholesterol-lowering medication such as a statin, and if so, did you stop it and why?
subjective.why_it_matters: Prior statin intolerance or discontinuation narrows available therapeutic options and changes the management pathway.

subjective.vernacular: Do you have irregular periods, excess facial or body hair, or acne that has been hard to control?
subjective.why_it_matters: Patient has known PCOS (E28.2), which is associated with insulin resistance and dyslipidemia including elevated LDL and triglycerides.
subjective.value: PCOS diagnosed 2005; active symptom status not documented
subjective.missing: Current PCOS symptom activity and treatment status

subjective.vernacular: Do you have any unexplained muscle aches, cramps, or weakness, particularly in your thighs or upper arms?
subjective.why_it_matters: Pre-existing myalgia is a contraindication-modifying factor for statin choice and dosing; baseline status must be known before starting therapy.

subjective.vernacular: How often are you taking ibuprofen, and for what reason?
subjective.why_it_matters: Regular NSAID use in a person with elevated BP raises cardiovascular risk and may interact with future lipid-lowering or antihypertensive therapy.
subjective.value: Ibuprofen listed as OTC medication (2026-07-01, two entries); frequency and indication unknown
subjective.missing: Frequency, dose, and reason for ibuprofen use

subjective.vernacular: What makes it hardest for you to follow through with medical appointments or take medications every day?
subjective.why_it_matters: Patient has documented social anxiety disorder, mobility limitations, and transportation challenges — all of which affect adherence to any treatment plan.
subjective.value: Social anxiety disorder, mobility and transportation challenges documented; adherence history unknown
subjective.missing: Impact on medication adherence and prior engagement with lipid management

objective.vernacular: Low-density lipoprotein (bad cholesterol) level from blood test

objective.term: Full fasting lipid panel — HDL, triglycerides, total cholesterol, non-HDL
objective.vernacular: Complete cholesterol profile including good cholesterol and fats in the blood
objective.missing: HDL, triglycerides, total cholesterol, and non-HDL values not available in record

objective.value: 195/194 mmHg (2026-07-03, FHIR); 120/60 mmHg (2026-06-13, self-reported) — marked discrepancy
objective.missing: Confirmed repeat measurement by clinician; the 195/194 reading is critically elevated and requires urgent clarification

objective.vernacular: A number calculated from height and weight that estimates healthy weight range
objective.value: Height 220 cm (2021), Weight 185 lbs / 83.9 kg (2026-06-14); calculated BMI approximately 17.4 — appears implausible given prior overweight diagnosis; data quality uncertain
objective.missing: Verified current height and weight in the same encounter; prior diagnosis of overweight (resolved 2026-07-03) conflicts with calculated BMI

objective.vernacular: Blood test that checks whether the thyroid gland is working properly
objective.missing: Not in record — required to exclude hypothyroidism as secondary cause

objective.vernacular: Blood sugar tests that check for diabetes or pre-diabetes
objective.value: HbA1c 5.1% (2019-05-28) — normal at that time; no recent result
objective.missing: Current fasting glucose and HbA1c; PCOS and prior overweight increase diabetes risk

objective.vernacular: Blood tests checking liver health (ALT, AST, bilirubin)
objective.missing: Required as baseline before statin initiation and to exclude secondary causes such as liver disease

objective.vernacular: Blood tests showing how well the kidneys are filtering waste
objective.missing: Chronic kidney disease is a cardiovascular risk enhancer and can cause secondary dyslipidemia

objective.vernacular: A calculated score estimating the chance of heart attack or stroke in the next 10 years
objective.how_obtained: calculated from age, sex, race, BP, cholesterol, smoking, diabetes, BP treatment
objective.missing: Cannot be calculated without complete lipid panel, confirmed BP, smoking status, and diabetes status

objective.vernacular: A CT scan that measures calcium deposits in the heart arteries to detect silent plaque buildup
objective.missing: Indicated if 10-year risk is borderline (5–20%) and decision about statin therapy is uncertain

objective.term: Androgen and sex hormone panel (testosterone, SHBG, LH/FSH)
objective.vernacular: Blood tests measuring hormone levels related to the ovaries and menstrual cycle
objective.missing: Relevant to PCOS activity, which drives insulin resistance and dyslipidemia

objective.vernacular: Ultrasound of the heart done in 2023 — the actual findings are not in the record
objective.value: TTE performed 2023-06-02; report present but findings/interpretation not extractable from record
objective.missing: Actual echocardiographic findings (EF, wall motion, valvular disease)

objective.vernacular: A special type of cholesterol particle that independently raises heart disease risk
objective.missing: Once-in-lifetime measurement recommended by ACC/AHA as a risk-enhancer; especially relevant if FH is suspected

assessment_candidates.vernacular: High cholesterol caused mainly by diet and inactivity, not a genetic condition
not_yet_testable: o-009 (10-year ASCVD risk score — not calculated)
assessment_candidates.basis: Most common cause of mildly-to-moderately elevated LDL in adults; prior overweight diagnosis and nutrition-related goals support lifestyle contribution.
assessment_candidates.confidence_note: Likely but cannot be confirmed without ruling out secondary causes; dietary data not formally documented.
assessment_candidates.severity_vernacular: If not addressed, accumulating plaque in arteries over years raises risk of heart attack or stroke — serious but preventable with lifestyle change and/or medication.

assessment_candidates.vernacular: High cholesterol driven by the hormonal and metabolic effects of polycystic ovary syndrome
not_yet_testable: o-002 (full lipid panel including triglycerides — absent)
assessment_candidates.basis: PCOS (confirmed ICD-10 E28.2) is strongly associated with insulin resistance, elevated LDL, elevated triglycerides, and low HDL; patient has had PCOS since 2005.
assessment_candidates.confidence_note: Real possibility given confirmed PCOS diagnosis; cannot quantify contribution without current hormonal and metabolic labs.
assessment_candidates.severity_vernacular: PCOS-related metabolic syndrome accelerates cardiovascular disease risk; untreated insulin resistance and dyslipidemia together cause lasting vessel damage.

assessment_candidates.vernacular: High cholesterol caused by an underactive thyroid gland slowing the body's ability to clear cholesterol
assessment_candidates.basis: Hypothyroidism is the most common secondary cause of elevated LDL; reduced thyroid hormone decreases LDL receptor activity; must be excluded before labeling as primary hypercholesterolemia.
assessment_candidates.confidence_note: No symptoms or TSH available — cannot rule in or out without testing.
assessment_candidates.severity_vernacular: If missed, treating cholesterol without treating the thyroid will be ineffective; hypothyroidism itself causes fatigue, cardiac effects, and other morbidity.

assessment_candidates.vernacular: A genetic condition causing very high cholesterol from birth due to faulty LDL receptors
assessment_candidates.basis: FH affects 1 in 250 persons; LDL of 158 mg/dL is in the range seen in heterozygous FH, particularly in women; Dutch Lipid Clinic Network criteria require family history and physical exam findings.
assessment_candidates.confidence_note: LDL alone is insufficient to diagnose FH; family history and physical exam findings are essential and absent from the record.
assessment_candidates.severity_vernacular: Untreated FH causes premature heart attack often before age 50; aggressive early statin therapy is life-saving and delays are irreversible.

assessment_candidates.vernacular: The combination of high cholesterol and severely elevated blood pressure creating a much higher heart attack and stroke risk than either alone
assessment_candidates.basis: The 2026-07-03 FHIR reading of 195/194 mmHg, if confirmed, represents hypertensive crisis; combined with LDL 158 mg/dL this synergistically raises ASCVD risk and may change management urgency substantially.
assessment_candidates.confidence_note: The BP reading is extreme and may reflect measurement error; it is clinically untenable to ignore without verified repeat measurement.
assessment_candidates.severity_vernacular: If BP is truly this elevated alongside high cholesterol, the short-term risk of stroke or heart attack is critically high and requires immediate evaluation.

assessment_candidates.vernacular: Cholesterol raised or worsened by medications the person is taking
assessment_candidates.basis: Regular NSAID use does not directly raise LDL but impairs renal prostaglandins, can raise BP, and may mask pain that would otherwise prompt activity; chronic use warrants documentation; other medications not in record may be relevant.
assessment_candidates.confidence_note: Medication list is incomplete; primary effect of NSAIDs on LDL is indirect; this candidate is low probability for direct causation but important for risk contextualization.
assessment_candidates.severity_vernacular: Unrecognized drug contributions to cardiovascular risk delay the right treatment and may cause avoidable harm.

residual.vernacular: Something not on this list — the differential is never closed

plan_options.term: Urgent BP verification and hypertensive crisis evaluation
plan_options.vernacular: Repeat blood pressure measurement in clinic — the reading of 195/194 mmHg must be confirmed or refuted immediately before any other management decisions
plan_options.basis: ACC/AHA 2017 Hypertension Guidelines: BP ≥180/120 mmHg requires same-day evaluation; a systolic of 195 with diastolic of 194 approaches hypertensive emergency territory.
plan_options.who_can_act: Primary care clinician, urgent care provider, or emergency department

plan_options.term: Fasting lipid panel (complete) and metabolic workup
plan_options.vernacular: Blood tests to see the full cholesterol picture — including good cholesterol, triglycerides, liver function, kidney function, thyroid, and blood sugar
plan_options.basis: ACC/AHA 2018 Cholesterol Guidelines require complete fasting lipid panel, TSH, glucose/HbA1c, LFTs, and renal function before initiating therapy and to exclude secondary causes.
plan_options.who_can_act: Primary care clinician or ordering clinician

plan_options.term: Therapeutic lifestyle change counseling — dietary and physical activity
plan_options.vernacular: Working with a dietitian and starting a heart-healthy diet (less saturated fat, more fiber) and regular exercise, which are always the first step regardless of medication decisions
plan_options.basis: ACC/AHA 2018 Cholesterol Guidelines: lifestyle therapy is first-line for all patients with elevated LDL; patient already has active nutrition and activity goals (2024-07-08).
plan_options.who_can_act: Primary care clinician, registered dietitian, or care coordinator

plan_options.vernacular: Using a validated calculator to estimate the 10-year chance of heart attack or stroke, which determines whether medication is recommended
plan_options.basis: ACC/AHA 2018 Guideline on Management of Blood Cholesterol: PCE calculation is required to guide statin therapy decisions in primary prevention.
plan_options.who_can_act: Primary care clinician (requires complete lipid panel, confirmed BP, smoking status, and diabetes status)

plan_options.term: Familial hypercholesterolemia screening (Dutch Lipid Clinic Network criteria)
plan_options.vernacular: Asking structured questions about family history of early heart disease and checking for physical signs of cholesterol deposits to see if a genetic cause is likely
plan_options.basis: EAS/ESC FH Guidelines 2019: clinical scoring using DLCN criteria should be applied when LDL is elevated, especially if family history is unknown.
plan_options.who_can_act: Primary care clinician or lipid specialist

plan_options.vernacular: A single blood test to check whether the thyroid is underactive, which is a treatable cause of high cholesterol
plan_options.basis: Standard workup for secondary hypercholesterolemia recommended by ACC/AHA and Endocrine Society guidelines.

plan_options.term: PCOS metabolic reassessment — insulin resistance, androgens, and current lipid profile
plan_options.vernacular: Updated blood tests to see how the ovary condition (PCOS) is affecting cholesterol and blood sugar now, since the last test was in 2019
plan_options.basis: Endocrine Society 2023 PCOS Guidelines recommend periodic metabolic screening including fasting glucose, HbA1c, and lipid panel given ongoing cardiovascular risk.

plan_options.term: Statin therapy initiation (moderate-intensity) — shared decision-making discussion
plan_options.vernacular: A conversation with the care team about whether to start a cholesterol-lowering pill (statin), weighing benefits and side effects together
plan_options.basis: ACC/AHA 2018 Guideline: shared decision-making is recommended before initiating statin therapy in primary prevention; decision depends on 10-year risk, risk enhancers, and patient preference.
plan_options.who_can_act: Primary care clinician in partnership with the patient; adherence support needed given documented anxiety and access barriers

plan_options.vernacular: A one-time blood test for a special cholesterol particle that independently raises heart disease risk and may point toward a genetic cause
plan_options.basis: ACC/AHA 2018 and NLA 2023 recommend Lp(a) measurement as a lifetime once test for risk enhancement assessment, especially when LDL is elevated or FH is suspected.

plan_options.term: Care coordination with telehealth or home-based services
plan_options.vernacular: Arranging phone or video visits and possibly home BP monitoring to reduce barriers from anxiety, mobility limitations, and transportation challenges
plan_options.basis: Patient's documented social anxiety disorder, mobility and transportation barriers make in-person follow-up difficult; telehealth reduces dropout and improves chronic disease management in this population.
plan_options.who_can_act: Care coordinator, social worker, or primary care team
